newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIA GOVT PAPER SEEN DOWN ON FOREIGN DEMAND WED.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIA GOVT PAPER SEEN DOWN ON FOREIGN DEMAND WED.

text.p: A possible flow of fresh foreign funds and the low volumes of roubles needed for repayment of maturing paper may could push yields down on Russian government paper at Wednesday's auctions, dealers said on Tuesday.
*Central bank sold 176 bln rbls of bills, bonds

Dealers forecast the average yield for the 182-day T-bill would be in the 17.34-18.61 percent range. Series 23002 T-bills, maturing on February 18, 1998, the closest maturity date to the new issue, closed at 91.20 to yield 18.54 percent.

Dealers forecast the average yield for 364-day T-bill would be in the 18.93-19.17 percent range. Series 21083 T-bills, maturing on August 5, 1998, the closest maturity date to the new issue, closed at 84.27, to yield 19.03 percent.

"We are expecting big demand from non-residents on non-competitive bids -- in such cases the Finance Ministry has a wide choice and in effect sets the auction price," International Moscow Bank dealer Yevgeny Krayev said.
"If it needs money it will sell at a premium, if not, the average yield for the one-year paper will be at about 18.80 percent."

But Raiffeisen Bank Austria's Alexander Losev said he did not expect much money from foreigners as they were holding their investments until the autumn, when Russia's international credit rating may be revised.
"August is not the month when big money comes in," he said. "Maybe the non-residents who are repaid tomorrow will re-invest the funds as the current hard currency yields on them are attractive."
